cards.front: Recall a key point about Selection of Materials and Components
cards.back: Selection criteria: function, aesthetics, cost (material + processing + assembly), availability, sustainability (recyclability, material miles), manufacturability.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Selection of Materials and Components
cards.back: Decision matrix: weighted scoring system - list criteria, assign weights, score each option, multiply weight x score, total reveals best choice. Removes bias.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Selection of Materials and Components
cards.back: Working properties must match function: frying pan handle needs thermal insulation (thermoset/silicone), not conductivity (metal). Bicycle frame needs strength-to-weight (aluminium/CFRP).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Selection of Materials and Components
cards.back: Batch vs mass production affects material choice: mass production justifies injection moulding tooling; batch uses CNC or hand-laid composites.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Selection of Materials and Components
cards.back: Environmental considerations: full life cycle - extraction, processing, use phase, end of life. Cradle-to-cradle design aims for zero waste.

cards.front: What should you know about d&t exam tips?
cards.back: For material selection: 1) Identify relevant criteria, 2) Weight by importance, 3) Score each option, 4) Total and compare, 5) State justified conclusion. This demonstrates AO3 evaluation.
Can it do the job? (e.g. Performance testing)
Does it look right? (e.g. Visual/colour matching)
Can it be made as designed? (e.g. Process feasibility)
Is it within budget? (e.g. Supplier quotes)
Is it environmentally responsible? (e.g. LCA, certifications)
Can it be sourced reliably? (e.g. Supplier stock check)

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: The cheapest material is always the best choice because it maximises profit. Correct: Initial cost is only one factor. A cheap material may fail in use (warranty claims), require expensive processing, have limited availability, or be unsustainable.
